## Molar masses from composition strings (`composition`) {#sec-ch02-molar-mass}

### Summary

kintera never takes a molar mass from the user. It computes each species' molar mass from its elemental
composition, written in the YAML file as a map from element symbol to count. This keeps mass and moles consistent
across every conversion between mass fractions and mole fractions (@sec-ch03-thermo-y).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $\mu_n = \sum_e a_{en} m_e$, @eq-ch02-molar-mass-sum.

**Data.** `composition: {H: 2, O: 1}` in; $\mu_n$ [kg mol$^{-1}$] out.

**Placement.** Once per species, when the registry is filled (@sec-ch02-species-registry).

**Activation.** Always; `composition` is required for every species.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact sum; the element masses come from the pyharp element table.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $\mu_n$, molar mass of species $n$ [kg mol$^{-1}$]; $a_{en}$, number of atoms of element $e$ in
species $n$ [-]; $m_e$, atomic mass of element $e$ [kg mol$^{-1}$].

### Derivation

The molar mass is the composition-weighted sum of atomic masses:

$$
\mu_n = \sum_e a_{en}\, m_e .
$$ {#eq-ch02-molar-mass-sum}

@eq-ch02-molar-mass-sum is evaluated by `molar_mass` ({{< code src/utils/molar_mass.cpp molar_mass >}}), which
calls the pyharp compound-weight function; kintera stores the result as kg mol$^{-1}$, the unit `ThermoY` assumes
when it forms $1/\mu_n$ in mol kg$^{-1}$. `atomic_mass` ({{< code src/utils/molar_mass.cpp atomic_mass >}})
converts a single element's mass from g mol$^{-1}$ to kg mol$^{-1}$ by the factor $10^{-3}$. The internals of the
pyharp table are not read for this section.

A second entry point, `molar_masses_from_yaml` ({{< code src/utils/molar_mass.cpp molar_masses_from_yaml >}}),
reads a chemistry file with `phases` and `species` and returns the molar masses in phase order, for the
equilibrium solver of @sec-ch05. The composition-string parser `parse_comp_string`
({{< code src/utils/parse_comp_string.cpp parse_comp_string >}}) reads strings such as `"H:2, O:1"`; at the pin
the species reader does not use it (it reads the YAML map directly), only the photochemistry cross-section loader
does (verified by reading the callers).

### Numerical method

No numerical method: one sum per species, done once at load time.

The molar-mass figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| species molar mass | {{< code src/utils/molar_mass.cpp molar_mass >}} | `molar_mass` | `composition` |
| element mass | {{< code src/utils/molar_mass.cpp atomic_mass >}} | `atomic_mass` | always |
| from a chemistry file | {{< code src/utils/molar_mass.cpp molar_masses_from_yaml >}} | `molar_masses_from_yaml` | `phases`, `species` |
| from element matrix | {{< code src/utils/molar_mass.cpp molar_masses >}} | `molar_masses` | API |
| composition strings | {{< code src/utils/parse_comp_string.cpp parse_comp_string >}} | `parse_comp_string` | API |

: Code map of the molar masses. {#tbl-ch02-molar-mass-code}

Setup checks a user can hit: `molar_masses_from_yaml` refuses a file without `phases` or `species`, a species with
no `name` or `composition`, a duplicate species and a phase component with no definition; `molar_masses` refuses a
component with no positive molar mass; `parse_comp_string` refuses duplicate keys and unparsable pairs.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_species_registry.py` | molar masses of a second card equal its reference values | $10^{-12}$ rel. | not yet derived |
| `test_kinetics_base_units.py` | molar masses from a KINETICS-base input are in kg mol$^{-1}$ | $10^{-3}$ rel. | element table rounded to 0.01 g mol$^{-1}$ (test docstring) |

: Tests of the molar masses. {#tbl-ch02-molar-mass-tests}

The tolerances are read from the test files at the pin. No test checks @eq-ch02-molar-mass-sum against hand values
for a YAML card: missing evidence.

### Limits

The element table belongs to pyharp, so its values and their precision are outside this report; an element pyharp
does not know cannot be used. Isotopes and non-integer compositions are accepted as given (the counts are read as
floating-point numbers).
